title: The Last Work Light
author: Agile Lens
source: Original text created for the Understudy sample pack, October 28, 2026. Not a quotation or a device-readiness claim.

entries.text: Original rehearsal text. Pause and resume at your own pace.
Leave that light on for a minute. I know the room is empty. That is why I can finally hear it.
Yesterday there were twelve people here telling me where to stand. Tonight the floor has stopped giving orders.
This mark is where I said goodbye. Two feet to the left is where I meant it. That is a small distance until you have to cross it.
My father built sets. He could make a painted door sound like oak, but he could never leave a real door without checking the latch.
I used to think that was fear. Now I think it was care. Someone had to know the room would hold after everyone went home.
Tomorrow I will walk out there and say the line. I will probably put the emphasis in the wrong place. People survive that.
What I cannot do is wait until I am certain. Certainty has missed every rehearsal we invited it to.
All right. Turn it off. I know where the door is now.
